\begin{chapstatus}{The thread of this chapter}
Bits mean nothing by themselves: a code gives them a meaning, and the same 32 bits can be a number, a colour, four letters or an instruction. Next: the codes for integers, and what happens when they run out of bits.
\par\medskip\textbf{Exit ticket} (two to four minutes, alone, on paper):
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=2em]
\item A mercury thermometer and a display that shows 21.5 both measure temperature. Which is analog and which digital? Why can the digital reading be copied a thousand times without getting worse?
\item The Undo button of an editor cancels the most recent change first, then the one before. Which of the five data structures fits, and why not an array reached by index?
\end{enumerate}
\end{chapstatus}
